subject.title: plugins update can downgrade/pin stale plugin version instead of latest available version

question: For targeted plugin id updates with a stale exact npm install record and a newer active plugin copy, should OpenClaw preserve exact-pin semantics and only block/warn on downgrades, or automatically move the plugin to the registry default/latest line?
rationale: Current docs and recent merged PRs intentionally preserve exact pins for `plugins update <id>`, while this issue's acceptance criteria ask the id form to resolve latest in at least this stale-record scenario.

options.title: Guard downgrades, keep pins
options.body: Preserve the documented exact-pin contract, but make `plugins update <id>` fail or skip when the recorded target would downgrade the active plugin and show the explicit `package@latest` or exact-version command to proceed.

options.title: Follow registry default
options.body: Change targeted id updates to choose the latest/default registry target when the active plugin is newer than the tracked record, accepting a broader behavior change from current docs.

options.title: Keep current behavior
options.body: Leave exact pins fully authoritative even when they reactivate an older copy, relying on explicit package specs and manual verification for recovery.

recommendation.title: Guard downgrades, keep pins
recommendation.body: Preserve the documented exact-pin contract, but make `plugins update <id>` fail or skip when the recorded target would downgrade the active plugin and show the explicit `package@latest` or exact-version command to proceed.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses plugin updater semantics, update-channel policy, and current docs that recent history ties to this owner area.
